leftEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.
points.right: A father asks mercy for his suffering son after the disciples fail to cure him; Jesus rebukes the demon and the boy is healed.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.
points.right: Jesus answers the disciples about their little faith and then again predicts betrayal, death, and resurrection.

payload.posture: Matthew carries the same disciples from divine voice and fear into a father’s appeal and failed healing.

rightEvidence.role: From glory into distress and another death prediction
rightEvidence.title: A father’s appeal follows the mountain vision

payload.tension: The valley exposes little faith and another death prediction without undoing what was seen above.
payload.title: Glory above and failed healing below
